assertions.name: nz_series_is_odd_only_every_even_coefficient_vanishes
assertions.source: largest |a_even| = 7.08086e-41 against smallest |a_odd| = 3.10912e-5 -- NZ eq (52) states c_n = 0 for even n, and this VERIFIES it on the computed series rather than imposing it. It is what makes the leading correction to tau second order in u, which is the whole quantitative point of this probe

assertions.name: tau_zero_is_two_sqrt_minus_three
assertions.source: c_1 = (0.0 + 3.4641016151377545871j) against the closed form 2 sqrt(-3) = (0.0 + 3.4641016151377545871j), agreeing to 4.59177e-41. This is the figure-eight cusp shape at the COMPLETE structure and is read out of NZ's gluing equations here, not assumed from the literature value

assertions.name: c3_over_tau_zero_is_exactly_one_third_matching_NZ_68
assertions.source: c_3/c_1 = (0.3333333333333333333333 + 0.0j) against 1/3, agreeing to 5.73972e-42. NZ eq (68) shows 1/3 at this slot for 4_1, so the series inversion reproduces the published coefficient independently. tau(u) = 2 sqrt(-3) (1 + u^2/3 + O(u^4))

assertions.name: the_NZ_cusp_shape_is_an_exact_integer_point_of_the_corpus_lattice
assertions.source: 2 sqrt(-3) = -2 + 4 omega to 2.29589e-41. The corpus states the 4_1 cusp lattice as hexagonal Z<1, omega> (cusp-shape-bar-parity.md, proved); NZ state the cusp SHAPE as 2 sqrt(-3). Not a tension and not the same statement -- the NZ meridian-longitude lattice Z<1, tau_0> is the index-4 sublattice (det [[1,0],[-2,4]] = 4) of the shortest-vector one. Two independent sources agreeing on one lattice, with an EXACT integer relation rather than a numerical one

assertions.name: the_meridian_normalisation_binary_is_carried_not_settled
assertions.source: both branches computed and NEITHER adopted: u = ln q0 drifts tau by 0.003629 and u = 2 ln q0 by 0.014516, a ratio of exactly 4 because the factor enters tau squared. Which branch is correct is the same factor of two as bean qou-yh67's NZ-1/2 binary (kappa_shape = sqrt3/2 against kappa_pot = sqrt3/4, the Phi = 2 V factor), and qou-yh67 records that it CANNOT be settled numerically. Choosing the branch that lands a target would be selection against the target under the anti-fit rule, so no choice is made here

assertions.name: the_derived_modulus_drift_is_second_order_not_first
assertions.source: the largest DERIVED energy shift is 0.00637123 against 0.0429233 for the O(u) drift I picked by hand. NZ's odd series [A1] forces the leading tau correction to be u^2, so the real sensitivity is quadratically suppressed. CORRECTS my own uncommitted measurement, which drifted omega at the O(u) = 10.4% scale in three directions and reported 3.9-16.3% energy shifts as the bridge's modulus sensitivity. Those numbers were correct for the drifts I chose and wrong about the drift the framework actually has

assertions.name: the_bridge_energies_are_robust_to_the_real_modulus_drift
assertions.source: the O'Hara energy of the (2,3) class moves by 0.00637123 between the complete structure and the deformed cusp, on the WORSE of the two normalisation branches. So the bridge probe's figures, computed at omega, are good at the sub-percent to few-percent level and its ranking cannot be an artefact of evaluating at u = 0. This answers the concern qbeta_cusp_shape_drift_robustness_probe raises without needing the binary above resolved -- both branches clear it

assertions.name: no_modulus_can_fix_the_bridge_order_blindness
assertions.source: the class (m, l) = (writhe, strands) is computed from the word and the closure ALONE -- the modulus enters only afterwards, when the class is turned into a geodesic. So deforming tau rescales every candidate's energy together and can never separate two words that share a class. This is structural, not numerical: it holds for every tau, including ones outside the NZ family. The bridge's negative therefore survives this correction intact -- what moved is the size of the modulus uncertainty, not the blindness

description: Derives the figure-eight cusp shape tau(u) = c_1 + c_3 u^2 + ... from Neumann-Zagier's own gluing equations (65)-(66) by series-inverting u(v), and gets tau_0 = 2 sqrt(-3) with c_3/c_1 = 1/3 exactly, matching NZ (68). Cross-checks that against the corpus's hexagonal cusp lattice: 2 sqrt(-3) = -2 + 4 omega exactly, so the NZ meridian-longitude lattice is the index-4 sublattice of Z<1, omega> -- two sources, one lattice, exact integer relation. CORRECTS my own earlier measurement of the O'Hara bridge's modulus sensitivity: the derived drift is O(u^2) and ~0.36% (or ~1.45% on the other normalisation branch), not the ~10% I drifted omega by hand, so the bridge's energies are robust at the sub-percent level. The meridian-normalisation binary u = ln q0 vs u = 2 ln q0 is the NZ-1/2 factor of bean qou-yh67 and is CARRIED, not settled -- both branches are reported and neither adopted. The bridge's order-blindness survives: the class (m, l) = (writhe, strands) never references the modulus, so no tau can make this embedding order-sensitive.

nz_coefficients.source: NZ (65)-(66) series-inverted; (52) odd-only verified; (68) shows the 1/3

normalisation_binary.why_not_settled: qou-yh67 records that the NZ-1/2 factor cannot be settled numerically; picking the branch that lands a target is selection against the target
normalisation_binary.note: both branches clear the robustness check, so the bridge's conclusion does not depend on which is right

corrects.my own uncommitted modulus measurement: I drifted omega at the O(u) = 10.4% scale in three hand-picked directions and reported 3.9-16.3% energy shifts as the bridge's modulus sensitivity. NZ's odd series makes the real drift O(u^2), so the derived shift is 0.00637123 -- an order of magnitude smaller. The old numbers were right about the drifts I chose and wrong about the drift the framework has

scope.class: (a) scope-limited -- the 4_1 cusp, the NZ family of deformations, one geodesic class

that omega(u) := (tau(u)+2)/4 is derived -- it is the natural continuation of the shortest-vector basis under a deformation fixing the meridian, and is a DEFINITION
that the O'Hara energy cannot select -- this concerns one embedding's blindness, not the functional
